symptom: Every `TestGitMerge_*` fixture and both real-mx `TestGitMergeIntegration_*` tests fail on a host named `vm` with `Committer identity unknown … unable to auto-detect email address (got 'root@vm.(none)')`, before the command under test runs; they pass on CI runners and developer machines
cause: The fixtures drop the global git config (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null) for hermeticity, but `gitInE` and the command's own in-process `git merge`/`git commit` in the integration fixture ran without the fixed identity `gitIn` sets, so git fell back to guessing one from the hostname — which works wherever the hostname has a domain
file: `cmd/mxcli/gitdoctor_test.go` (`gitInE` sets GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_*), `cmd/mxcli/gitmerge_integration_test.go` (`mergeIntegrationRepo` sets them in the process environment)
insight: **Removing the global config is half of hermetic**: git still guesses an identity from the hostname, so a fixture that never sets one passes exactly where the hostname has a domain — every runner image and laptop — and fails in a bare container. `git merge` needs the identity even when it stops on a conflict. Pattern: docs-wiki/bug-patterns/the-platform-ci-does-not-run.md
